5.0.s.en: (1) Love and the rejection of fornication and covetousness

5.0.0.en: The Apostle asks the people of Ephesus to imitate God in His love for us, because we are His children who love Him.

5.1.0.en: Let us not have feelings of love only, but let them be turned into practical conduct in our love for one another, so that our love is self-giving, as Christ gave Himself for us in obedience to God the Father. For the sake of our love for God we sacrifice our lives in the service of others, counting our life the least thing we offer to God as a sacrifice of love, because of His surpassing love for us, so that our life rises as a sweet savor before Him and He rejoices in it.

5.2.0.en: All uncleanness: all kinds of fornication and perversion.

5.2.1.en: Covetousness: love of money and possessions.

5.2.2.en: Let it not once be named: do not mention their names, and let none of the believers be characterized by them.

5.2.3.en: The Apostle forbids fornication of every kind, and likewise love of money and covetousness for the material things of the world. He does not want them spoken of among the holy believers, that is, those set apart for God, and no one is to be called by these evil sins.

5.3.0.en: Filthiness: mocking talk about sexual matters.

5.3.1.en: Foolish talking and jesting: venting grumbling in words of mockery and trivialities.

5.3.2.en: The people of Ephesus were known for joking that included unclean talk and useless jesting, as a way of venting any distress they suffered. So the Apostle warns them to leave what they were known for, and even calls them to give thanks to God for His gifts that overwhelm them.

5.4.0.en: An idolater: the fornicator makes lust his god and the covetous man makes money his god, so both are counted idolaters.

5.4.1.en: The Apostle warns us against evil lusts and love of money, whose end is eternal torment, so that we repent of them and leave them.

5.4.2.en: Your goal is love of God, which appears in love for all those around you, and by this you leave the love of sin and the lusts of this passing world. In proportion to the service you offer to those around you, you rescue yourself and keep it far from sin, since love for others takes the place of selfishness and satisfying the soul with the pleasures of sin.

5.5.s.en: (2) Children of darkness and children of light

5.5.0.en: The Apostle warns the believers against what the pagans promote of ideas that match the pagan view of morals and conduct, namely that fornication and uncleanness are natural matters and do not defile the soul, while covetousness they regard as wisdom and not love of possession. The Apostle reinforces his warning against being deceived by those claims, because the wrath of God falls on those who commit these things, since they are rebels against God and disobey His commandments. So he forbids them to share in their sins and expose themselves to divine punishment.

5.6.0.en: Darkness is a figure for ignorance and misery, and it is the state the believers were in before their faith and their accepting Christ as Redeemer and Savior; after their faith they became enlightened and a source of blessing and light to others. Christ is the Sun of Righteousness and His disciples reflect His light on others when they walk as befits the children of God.

5.7.3.en: God's purpose concerning us is that His same exalted attributes appear in us, for the new nature He gave us inclines to doing good and all that is upright.

5.8.0.en: The children of the world seek what is pleasing to themselves, but the children of light make God's will the goal of every work they do or refrain from.

5.8.1.en: May we get used to asking ourselves before every deed: Does this deed of mine redound to the glory of the Lord? Is it what Christ wants from me? ... If I say this word or do this deed, shall I be fulfilling the will of my Master and Savior?

5.9.0.en: The works of darkness are those that the unbelieving person does because of the corruption of his heart and conscience, and they are unfruitful because they are of no benefit, indeed they are harmful to souls and expose them to eternal destruction. So the children of light must not share in them, and more than that, they should show by their words their disapproval of them, so that all may know how defiling and hideous they are.

5.10.0.en: Those who commit evil works fear the light, so they do them in secret, and they are so shameful that even to mention them is also shameful. So we must refrain from mentioning them.

5.11.0.en: All things: all the sins that are done in secret.

5.11.1.en: Whatsoever doth make manifest is light: every sin that we expose we are rid of, and our life is enlightened.

5.11.2.en: The Apostle shows the power of divine truth in the believers, because they rebuke the evils that the pagans do and so declare the truth, for Satan finds his opportunity in people's persisting in their evil when they hide their sins. But if a person faces himself, especially before spiritual people, the guilt of sin appears, so he repents of it and is enlightened by the light of God.

5.11.3.en: From here appears the importance of the sacrament of confession, when a person exposes his sins before his spiritual father, is rid of them and begins the struggle against them, especially when he is strengthened by partaking of the Holy Mysteries.

5.12.0.en: St. Paul the Apostle quoted this verse from (Isa 60:1), and the quotation here is by meaning and not by wording. The call is to awake from the sleep of heedlessness and from the death of sin, for it is a call to repentance and spiritual wakefulness, and when a person rises from spiritual death by the life-giving power of Christ, Christ lights the way for him, so that afterward he lives and walks in the light and no longer walks in darkness.

5.13.0.en: Walking circumspectly means walking with care and spiritual alertness, paying attention to the snares Satan may set in our path to make us fall into them. We must know how to take each step, for the wise man is not deceived, while the fool goes through this world without reckoning the consequences of things.

5.14.0.en: Redeeming the time: means making use of the time available to us in this life, so we do not waste it on behalf of the world but use it in doing good.

5.14.1.en: The days are evil: what is meant is the multitude of trials and dangers that surround a person during his temporal life; therefore we must seize every available opportunity to lay up treasures for ourselves in the Kingdom of Heaven by holy worship and good works.

5.14.2.en: The Apostle calls us to use every opportunity for life with God because of the many wars of the devil that try to hinder us from it.

5.14.3.en: The door is open before us today to serve the Lord and work for the abiding life, before the door is shut and we are like the foolish virgins when the door was shut before them. May we make a plan at the beginning of each day so that we use our time in a better way, and also examine ourselves at the end of each day to repent of our sins and guard against falling into them in the days that follow.

5.15.0.en: Do not act foolishly and without wisdom, but you must understand the will of the Lord for His children, which is that you walk in holiness, as the Apostle himself says in (1 Thess 4:3), "For this is the will of God, even your sanctification."

5.16.0.en: The Apostle warns against drunkenness with wine because the spirit of drunkenness dominates the actions of the drunkard and his words, which are then marked by debauchery and rioting, things that do not befit the children of light, whose conduct must be controlled by the Spirit of truth, that is, the Spirit of God, who produces all the fruits of the godly Christian life.

5.17.0.en: Those filled with the Holy Spirit delight in speaking of God, who takes pleasure in His own, so they speak to one another of His love and His grace. Prayer and praise with God's word in the psalms, hymns and spiritual songs also helps toward being filled with the Spirit, provided that all of it is from the heart and not merely with the lips.

5.18.0.en: The name of our Lord Jesus Christ: in the name of Christ we receive salvation and all spiritual blessings, just as we close the Lord's Prayer with the words "through Christ Jesus our Lord."

5.18.1.en: Our thanksgiving to God is always for the bodily and spiritual mercies He has bestowed on us in our past life and until now. And thanks is for everything, even what may seem painful to us, because we know that all things in the end work together for good, so we thank God for all His gifts which we have received and receive through Christ the Redeemer.

5.19.0.en: Thanksgiving makes us feel that what we enjoy is from God, so we humble ourselves before Him, and this leads us to humility before one another so that we learn the virtues of others. God is before us, so we fear Him and are not proud and we reject all evil, and this drives us to greater humility toward one another, so we bear with them, give them precedence in honor over ourselves and learn from them all that is good.

5.20.0.en: After the Apostle called all the believers to be humble and submit to one another, men and women alike, because humility is the characteristic of all believers and a proof of their love for one another, he here specifies his words and calls women to submit to their husbands. For the personality of man, as God created him, inclines to leadership, bearing responsibility and giving of himself for those he is responsible for, and for this leadership to be carried out the wife must submit to him, because the family needs one leader and there cannot be two, or else conflict arises and leadership cannot be carried out. And because the Christian man leads his family in the fear of God, the wife's submission to him is submission to God. This submission does not mean not giving her opinion or sharing in making decisions, nor does it mean domination and control by the man; rather it is an ordering of the work and the taking of decisions within the family, and it suits the psychology of the woman, who wishes to have a strong man who leads the family and on whom she can lean.

5.21.0.en: Christian marriage is an image of the glorious relationship between Christ and His Church. Just as Christ is the head of the Church, which is His body, so the Christian husband is the head of the wife. And just as Christ cared for the salvation and peace of the Church, so the husband must care for his wife's well-being and happiness; for this reason this position was given to him, and not to dominate her or to be harsh in dealing with her.

5.22.0.en: So in the likeness of, and to the measure of, the Church's submission to Christ is the measure of submission due from the wife to the husband.

5.22.1.en: In every thing: that is, it is not permitted for the wife to submit in some things and not do so in others. But this obedience is to be in the Lord, that is, she must not violate God's commandments in obeying her husband's command.

5.23.0.en: The Apostle presents Christ's love for the Church as an example which he asks men to imitate in their love for their wives. Christ loved the Church to the point of giving Himself for her, and so a man ought to love his wife with this giving love.

5.24.0.en: The purpose for which Christ loved the Church and gave Himself for her is to sanctify her, consecrate her and set her apart for Himself, by cleansing her from the sins of everyone who joins her membership, with the washing of water, that is, by immersion in the water of Baptism, and also by the word, that is, by faith in Christ.

5.25.1.en: Wrinkle: the corruption or alteration of a thing so that it is no longer good (like the creasing of a garment). By His redemption Christ gave salvation to His Church by renewing her nature through Baptism, and by this she regained her first glory in the garden of Eden and was rid of her evils and everything that corrupts her nature; indeed she became holy and set apart for life with Him. So the husband, by his love and self-giving, keeps every disturbance and evil away from his wife, and they live in one love with God.

5.26.0.en: Just as Christ, the head of the Church, gave Himself for the Church His body, so men should regard their wives as their bodies, that is, a part of themselves, so they love them and give everything for them. And by loving their wives they love themselves, because the two have become one. And just as no one is vexed with his body however many illnesses or pains it has, but takes care of it and attends to its needs, so the man must love his wife whatever faults or shortcomings she has, and even take care to complete and tend her, as Christ does with His Church.

5.27.0.en: As Christ nourishes His Church and brings her up, because she is His invisible body, the relation between Christ and His Church is like the relationship between Adam and Eve, for Eve was taken from the body of Adam and so is of his flesh and bone; likewise the wife is the body of the man, so he cares for it and tends it.

5.28.0.en: The Apostle quoted this verse from the Book of Genesis (Gen 2:24). The holy relationship between a man and his wife is closer than any other relationship, and the foundation on which each of the believers should build his relationship with his life partner is the permanent union between Christ and the Church.

5.29.0.en: The mystery: what the mind cannot reach to grasp.

5.29.1.en: What is meant by the mystery here is the union between the spouses, which is in the likeness of the union between Christ and the Church; it is not only one of the seven sacraments of the Church but also a deep union like the union of Christ with the Church.

5.30.0.en: The Apostle sums up the relationship of the spouses with one another: that the man love his wife as himself, and this is the first demand of all women, to be loved and always to hear expressions of love from their husbands. As for the woman's responsibility, it is to respect and esteem her husband, and this is the first demand of all men.

5.30.1.en: May every husband look on his wife as his church, so he loves her and gives his life for her as Christ did. And the wife looks on her husband as her Christ, so she loves him, submits to him and obeys him as the Church obeys the commandments of Christ.

6.0.s.en: (1) A commandment for parents and children

6.0.0.en: The duty of children is submission and obedience to their parents. Among the sins that St. Paul the Apostle mentioned of the pagan Gentiles is that they were "disobedient to parents" (Rom 1:29-31). "In the Lord" means that the children's obedience to their parents is obedience to Christ, provided that this obedience does not violate the will and commandments of the Lord. The reason that St. Paul the Apostle gives is "for this is right", and the meaning of that is that disobedience is evil.

6.1.0.en: In ancient times God gave the Ten Commandments. The first four commandments were not joined with a promise, but the fifth commandment, concerning honoring parents, is the first commandment with promise: "that thy days may be long upon the land" (Ex 20:12).

6.2.0.en: The reward of honoring parents may be length of physical days on earth, or length and abundance of happy days in which a person enjoys the blessings of God, even though his life is short in days.

6.2.1.en: May children obey their parents and honor them, so that they enjoy God's blessings and this beautiful promise is fulfilled for them: "that it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth." It is good to serve our parents, especially in their old age, in compensation for what they did for us.

6.3.0.en: Parents must beware of provoking their children by being harsh with them, for severe pressure on a young child causes him failure. So there must be love with firmness in dealing with children, along with disciplining them by making known to them the commandments of the Lord and bringing them up in a good religious upbringing.

6.3.1.en: May all parents sit often with their children and guide them well and know their hobbies and friends, and direct them to the teachings of the Holy Bible and to the Christian life. Every privilege is matched by a duty. Do we take care not to provoke our children, or do we only ask them to obey us??

6.4.0.en: The master according to the Spirit is Christ, while the master according to the flesh is the social position that existed at that time of masters and servants. So the Apostle commands servants that they ought to obey their masters with respect, obedience and great fear, and at the same time with pure hearts, not grumbling, full of love, as they feel toward Christ.

6.5.0.en: Eyeservice: is work done under observation.

6.5.1.en: Let the servants' service not be merely to please men, but let the servant do the work feeling that he is a servant of Christ Himself and offers the service to Christ and not as a slave to a man. In this way he is doing the will of God and carrying out His desire, expressing his love for Christ with all his heart.

6.6.0.en: Let the servants offer their bodily labor with good intention, counting the service and the toil as being for Christ and not for men.

6.7.0.en: Every good deed a person does, whether bond or free, he does not wait for his wages from men but receives his reward from the Lord.

6.8.0.en: The Apostle addresses the masters also, asking them to leave the manner of threatening in dealing with servants, warning them that they themselves are servants of a Master in heaven, who is Christ, who does not distinguish between one person and another because of his social position; with Him all are equal, and He judges among all with justice. By this he warns the believing masters so that they have the fear of the Lord. Thus Christianity raised the servants to the level of their masters, and afterward called for their liberation, so as not to cause social disorder had it begun by calling for the freeing of the slaves.

6.8.1.en: May you feel that you are dealing with God when you walk among people. Do not be troubled by insults, because God allowed them to correct your faults, and thank Him for every word of praise you hear from people, for it is encouragement from Him. And when you direct others, make sure that your words please God and are not from personal emotion. In this way you will feel God's presence with you, and He will bless your life.

6.9.0.en: We are weak in ourselves and our spiritual enemies, that is, the demons, are much stronger than we are, but by faith in the Lord and trust in Him we have sufficiency and the ability to overcome and be saved. However great the might of the enemy, Christ who is with us is stronger than he.

6.10.0.en: The devil our enemy does not war against us only in direct war, but uses many deceptions. So the Apostle asks us to prepare for him by putting on the spiritual weapons, which are complete, with no lack or gap, and include both defensive and offensive weapons, as we shall explain, so that we are able to stand against the enemy's attacks and even overcome him. And he says "put on", that is, the weapons are to be close to our bodies and cover us, so that it is no longer we who appear but Christ with whom we arm ourselves, and He is able of course to overcome the devil.

6.11.0.en: The darkness of this world: the evil prevalent in the world.

6.11.1.en: Spiritual wickedness in high places: that is, the demons were angels and fell, and their power is spiritual and not human, so it is loftier and stronger than the power of men.

6.11.2.en: The Apostle makes clear that our war is not easy because it is with the demons, who were angels of the orders of principalities and powers and rulers of the world, and fell. They have no authority except over the wicked, and because they are spirits their strength is greater than that of men, but when we arm ourselves with God we overcome them.

6.12.0.en: The whole armor of God: includes faith and all the practices of spiritual striving that the Church teaches us.

6.12.1.en: The evil day: the days of this life in which the devil attacks us with his evils.

6.12.2.en: Your nature is weak and the strength of your enemies is great, therefore take up the armor of God, for no other weapon can stand against the might of the enemies in the time of life in which we are exposed to temptation. And after you have armed yourselves with all the preparations and repelled all the attacks that come upon you, you remain firm, unshaken in the faith.

6.13.0.en: Stand before your enemies in the war. The girding of the loins above the waist is the first preparation for battle, and the girdle is Christ.

6.13.1.en: And the soldier's breastplate extends from the neck to the knee and protects the soldiers from the blow of the sword and the thrust of the arrow. What is meant here is that the perfect righteousness of Christ shields us from all external attacks, so we need only that our life be a life of practical righteousness, so that we give the enemy no entrance to the heart and conscience, by walking in the truth.

6.14.0.en: The Apostle calls us to walk by the word of the Holy Bible in our life, to protect us from every evil.

6.14.1.en: Shod: the soldier's boot is sometimes more important to him than the weapon in his hand, and without it he cannot move or run, especially on rough roads, for it protects him from thorns or slipping and falling.

6.14.2.en: The preparation of the gospel of peace: it is practical conduct in accordance with the teachings of the Gospel, such that our conduct is a living testimony to our peace with God, carrying the good news of grace and peace to souls far from Him. And the Gospel on which we depend enables us to pass through all difficulties, to tread on the thorns of the world and to climb over its rocks.

6.15.0.en: In addition to all the weapons mentioned we take up the shield: which was made of bronze, about a meter and a quarter long and three-quarters of a meter wide; the soldier fastens it to his left hand, and it protects the body from spears and arrows. And faith in the Christian struggle is like a shield, for by it we overcome the world and protect ourselves from its evils.

6.16.0.en: The helmet: a metal covering for the head that protects it from the enemy's weapons. The spiritual helmet is the helmet of salvation, that is, faith in Christ the Savior, who delivers our thoughts from evil and earthly things so that we think on heavenly things.

6.16.1.en: All the preceding weapons are for defense and protection, while the sword is for attack, and it is the soldier's tool for achieving victory and triumph over the enemies. What is meant by the sword here is the Holy Spirit, or the word of God which the Holy Spirit inspired in the writers of the divine books. There are no satanic devices that can shatter it and triumph over it. With the sword we cut off every sin within us, and it is double-edged, so it cuts off all kinds of sins.

6.16.2.en: May you always be ready, because the devil your enemy does not sleep. Hold fast to your faith and the word of God, taking care for your repentance every day, and you will be able to love everyone and seek peace with them, and so overcome the devil however great his power.

6.17.0.en: Supplication: is prayer for a particular matter.

6.17.1.en: To be strengthened in the Lord we must practice all the means of grace, among them prayer, since it keeps the Christian soldier in constant contact with the supreme Commander, the Lord Jesus Christ. We should pray at all times and not grow weary or be heedless. Our prayers will not be fervent and effective unless they are under the guidance of the Holy Spirit and His working in the heart. The believers are all one army, so the believer must not pray for himself only but for all the brethren also.

6.18.0.en: The mystery of the gospel: the salvation offered to all people, Gentiles and Jews, which the world did not know and the Jews did not believe.

6.18.1.en: He also asks them to pray for him, not that his chains be loosed and he be released from the prison in Rome, but that utterance be given to him, not in human wisdom but in the power of the Holy Spirit, when he preaches salvation to all people.

6.19.0.en: Although the Apostle was a prisoner in the prison of Rome and bound with chains, he counts himself an "ambassador" of the Gospel. While earthly ambassadors boast of the decorations they receive, the Apostle boasts of heavenly decorations, which are the chains with which he was bound. So he asks for their prayers that he may continue to proclaim the good news of Christ.

6.19.1.en: God will not look at the worldly honor we have received but at the faithfulness, godliness and conduct we have shown during our temporal life, and the sufferings, tribulations and trials we have borne with contentment and thanksgiving.

6.20.s.en: (5) The Apostle reassures the people of Ephesus and greets them

6.20.0.en: Because Paul was imprisoned in Rome, the believers in Ephesus were anxious about him, so he sent to them Tychicus, his disciple, to reassure them about his words.

6.21.0.en: As the Apostle sensed the longing of the believers for him and their desire to know his circumstances, he sent this epistle with Tychicus to comfort their hearts, and it was indeed a beautiful comfort in the truths and heavenly revelations it contained.

6.21.1.en: We should care about the feelings of others and take their concerns into account and not ignore them. So get used to offering words of encouragement and praise, and also to caring for those who worry about you, reassuring them even with a small word.

6.22.0.en: The Apostle Paul sends peace to the believers who commit their lives to the care of the blessed Father, and he asks God the Father and His Son Jesus Christ, the source of spiritual blessing, to fill their hearts with love in addition to the faith they have.

6.23.0.en: He closed the epistle with the apostolic blessing, in which he asks the grace of Christ for those who love Him and show this love by a pure life and walking in holiness.
